metadata.title: Stock market today: Dow and S&P 500 enter correction, Nasdaq sinks 5% to erase 2026 gains as AI trade melts down

content.text:
Stock market today: Dow and S&P 500 enter correction, Nasdaq sinks 5% to erase 2026 gains as AI trade melts down
US stocks tanked on Friday as a punishing sell-off deepened after Anthropic's (ANT) successful initial public offering failed to quell broad uncertainty about artificial intelligence safety and financing.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI) dropped 1.9% after the blue-chip index fell below 50,000 and neared a correction. The S&P 500 (^GSPC) declined by 3.6%. Both the Dow and S&P 500 closed in correction territory, or more than 10% off their peaks.
The Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC) fell nearly 5.3%, with the tech-heavy index closing negative for the year.
Investors went risk-off on Friday as semiconductor stocks led an AI trade sell-off. Nvidia (NVDA) shares extended losses, falling 14%. AMD (AMD), Broadcom (AVGO), and Micron (MU) stocks also suffered double-digit drops.
Yahoo Finance's Jared Blikre finds the damage beneath the Nasdaq Composite index is even worse. Seventy-one of the 101 stocks in the narrower Nasdaq-100 (^NDX) were in bear market territory on Friday, including 20 of the 20 semiconductor and memory chip stocks in that index.
A day after its record-breaking debut, Anthropic shares fell 8%, though they remain narrowly above their IPO price of $83. After a big pop on its IPO day, Anthropic faces a test in the markets to see whether it can sustain the momentum.
Other assets slid on Friday as well. Gold futures (GC=F) dropped nearly 4%, while the price of so-called digital gold — bitcoin (BTC-USD) — dropped below $59,000 to trade at its lowest price since July.
- Grace O'Donnell
Stocks suffer worst week of 2026, Dow has worst week since COVID era
Friday's sell-off was ugly, and it was the capstone to a losing week for Wall Street.
Our market statistician Jared Blikre ran the numbers for weekly losses, illustrating the damage to portfolios:
-
S&P 500: -8.6%, worst week since the "Liberation Day" sell-off in April 2025
-
Dow Jones Industrial Average: -8%, worst week since the COVID sell-off in March 2020
-
Nasdaq Composite: -10%, worst week since March 2020
-
Russell 2000: -7.5%, worst week since April 2025
-
Nvidia: -23%, worst week since October 2008
-
AMD: -20.5%, worst week since October 2018
-
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company: -20%, worst week since July 2002
-
- Ines Ferré
Nasdaq tanks 5% as the AI trade unravels, semiconductor stocks crash
Stocks tanked on Friday as the AI trade unraveled and semiconductor stocks crashed double-digit percentages.
The Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC) dropped more than 5.2%, fully erasing this year's gains. The tech-heavy index lost more than 1,200 points during the session as Nvidia (NVDA) stock dropped 14% and peers AMD (AMD) and Broadcom (AVGO) also sank.
Both the S&P 500 (^GSPC) and Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI) also sank to close in correction territory, or at least 10% off their peaks.
125.53 -20.45 (-14.01%)At close: November 20 at 4:00:01 PM EST130.01 +4.48 (+3.57%)After hours: 7:59:58 PM ESTNVDA AMD AVGO - David Hollerith
Wall Street's fear gauge hits highest level of 2026 as stocks plunge
Wall Street's fear gauge surged to its highest level of 2026 on Friday, as a deepening stock market sell-off rattled investors.
The Cboe Volatility Index, or VIX (^VIX), spiked briefly to 40 before easing. Its up more than 20% in afternoon trading, its highest level since April 2025 during the sweeping rollout of President Trump's Liberation Day tariff policy, according to Yahoo Finance data.
The index, which measures expectations for S&P 500 volatility over the next 30 days, is now nearly twice its 2026 average of 18.4. It has also surpassed its previous 2026 high set during the early innings of the US war in Iran.
The latest spike marks a dramatic reversal from just over a week ago, when the VIX hovered near its yearly average.
- Grace O'Donnell
Bonds rally as investors flee to safe havens
Treasurys are rallying as investors seek a safe haven from this week's volatility and eliminate bets that the Fed will enact a jumbo-sized rate hike in December.
The five-year Treasury yield fell 16 basis points to 4.70%.
The 10-year Treasury yield (^TNX) slid 13 basis points to 4.92%, its lowest level in over 10 days. For the week, the 10-year yield has fallen 4.5%.
The 30-year yield fell 9 basis points to 5.31%. Bond yields and prices move in opposite directions, meaning bond prices rose on Friday.
Bond traders also backtracked on growing bets that the Federal Reserve would raise rates by 50 basis points in December. They still largely expect the Fed to hike by 25 basis points (with 91.8% odds, according to CME Group), but now a contingent sees an 8% chance that the Fed holds rates steady, up from nil yesterday.
- Ines Ferré
Stocks near session lows, Nasdaq plunges as Nvidia sinks 12%
Stocks were trading near session lows with less than an hour left of trading. The Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC) was sinking 4.75%, on pace to erase this year's gains. The tech-heavy index has erased more than 1,000 points during the session.
Both the S&P 500 (^GSPC) and Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI) were on pace to close in a correction, at least 10% off their all-time high peaks.
Semiconductor stocks led the sell-off, with Nvidia (NVDA) down 12%. The stock is down more than 30% year-to-date. Peers AMD (AMD) and Broadcom (AVGO) also sank double-digit percentages.
424.39 -64.80 (-13.25%)At close: November 20 at 4:00:00 PM EST439.39 +15.00 (+3.53%)After hours: 7:59:58 PM ESTAMD NVDA AVGO - Grace O'Donnell
What is a correction and a bear market?
Friday's heavy losses have investors revisiting some terms thrown about in the bleakest of stock market days.
Correction: A correction is a sustained 10% drop in an index or other asset from a recent high.
The S&P 500 (^GSPC) and Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI) are on track to close in a correction. The S&P 500 has fallen 10.7% from its all-time closing high of 7,818.93 on Oct. 6, while the Dow has dropped 10.8% from its August record of 54,349.12. The Nasdaq-100 (^NDX) and Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC) entered correction territory in early November.
Bear market? A bear market is a prolonged decline in stock prices of 20% or more from a recent high.
The last bear market for stocks ended in 2022, but the Nasdaq-100 (^NDX) is in striking distance of closing in a new bear market today. The tech-heavy index is down roughly 19% from its October all-time high.
- David Hollerith
Chips are crashing like it's 2008 as the Nasdaq 100 nears a bear market
Wall Street is wrapping up a kind of week it has seen only five other times since World War II. Two of them came in 2008 and 2001, Yahoo Finance's Jared Blikre writes.
The S&P 500 (^GSPC) is on track to fall every day this week, with at least four drops of 1% or more. That has happened only in 1962, 1974, 1978, the week after the 9/11 attacks in 2001, and October 2008, according to Bespoke Investment Group.
Friday is seeing the strongest leg down. The S&P 500 is falling about 2% and the Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC) about 3.5%, enough to wipe out the Nasdaq's gain for 2026. The S&P 500 is shedding more than $1 trillion in market value on the day and is flirting with a correction, a close 10% below its Oct. 6 record. The Nasdaq 100 (^NDX) is closing in on a bear market, or a 20% drop from its record closing high.
- David Hollerith
Fed's Lisa Cook warns the Fed could get behind the curve if it doesn't raise rates now
Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook said Friday that the central bank risks getting behind the curve in bringing inflation down if it doesn't raise interest rates now, Yahoo Finance's Jennifer Schonberger reports:
"Inflation has been above target for more than five and a half years, and every additional day poses greater risk that price- and wage-setters will adjust their inflation expectations upward," Cook said in a speech in Santiago, Chile. "Waiting longer to implement rate increases risks getting behind the curve."
Cook dissented in October for the first time against the Fed's decision to hold rates steady.
Roughly all (97.5%) of traders expect the Fed to raise interest rates by 25 basis points after its upcoming December meeting, according the CME's Fedwatch tool.
- Grace O'Donnell
7 reasons why tech stocks are selling off, according to Dan Ives
In a note this morning, Yorkville Ives partner Dan Ives highlighted seven catalysts underpinning the sell-off in tech stocks this week.
"This sell-off has been driven by a perfect storm," Ives wrote. He listed the catalysts in his view for the latest tech rout:
-
"The Blue Tidal Wave win and fears about an anti-AI/anti-datacenter DC";
-
"Losing the global leader of the AI Revolution Jensen in his black eye moment";
-
"China driven regulatory concerns across the rest of semis/memory stocks (e.g. AMD short report yesterday)";
-
"Multiple market clearing events which have just led to more selling";
-
"Anthropic IPO being a massive success but marginally reducing liquidity from other tech names";
-
"Significant fund P&L pain diminishing buying power";
-
"Sticky inflation and hawkish Fed speak with concerns around more hikes and constricting financial conditions."
-
- Ines Ferré
Battered neocloud provider stocks extend declines
Neocloud providers battered over the past weeks took more pain on Friday.
Applied Digital (APLD) led the declines, down 16%, while IREN fell 12%. Nebius (NBIS) dropped 12.51%. CoreWeave (CRWV) also slid more than 9%, according to Yahoo Finance's AlphaSpace data.
- Grace O'Donnell
Gap stock jumps 12%. CEO says consumer is 'resilient but discerning.'
Amid a sea of red in markets today, there is one bright spot from a perhaps unlikely source. The Gap (GAP) stock is surging 12% and is on track for its best day of the year. On Thursday, the Old Navy and Banana Republic owner posted a narrow earnings beat but cut its full-year guidance.
Gap CEO Richard Dickson told Yahoo Finance's Brian Sozzi that he's expecting the holiday shopping season to hold up just fine.
"The consumer is resilient but discerning," Dickson said on Sozzi Unleashed.
- Ines Ferré
Chip stocks accelerate losses with double-digit declines over past week
Chip stocks tumbled on Friday as losses across the sector accelerated. Many of the market's high-flying chipmakers are now down double-digit percentages over the past week, as shown in Yahoo Finance's AlphaSpace.
Chip giant Nvidia (NVDA) fell 7% on Friday, putting its five-day losses at roughly 16%. Peers AMD (AMD) and Broadcom (AVGO) each dropped over 11% during the session, bringing AMD's weekly decline to about 19%.
Memory chipmaker Micron Technology (MU) dropped 13% on Friday, bringing its losses over the past five sessions to roughly 22%.
- Grace O'Donnell
Nasdaq falls 3%, may give back year-to-date gains
Brutal day on Wall Street, especially for tech investors. The Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC) has plunged over 3% to a session low, putting the tech-heavy index on pace to surrender its positive return for 2026.
The sell-off is concentrated in tech: The S&P 500 tech sector ETF (XLK) is down 5%, pulled lower by Broadcom (AVGO), Nvidia (NVDA), and AMD (AMD).
- David Hollerith
Consumer sentiment ticked up amid post-election optimism
November isn't shaping up to be a great month for stock investors but it isn't all bad. Consumer sentiment, per University of Michigan, has actually improved since the US midterm elections.
Yahoo Finance's Claire Boston reports:
Consumer sentiment ticked higher in November as consumers grew more confident about short-term and long-term business conditions following the election.
The University of Michigan's Consumer Sentiment Index rose 7.3% to 51.5 in November, from October's reading of 48. Economists expected a similarly sized improvement to 51.6.
- David Hollerith
Bitcoin falls below $60K as November woes deepen
Bitcoin (BTC-USD) plunged below $60,000 on Friday, deepening a November sell-off that is shaping up to be the largest cryptocurrency's worst monthly decline in more than four years.
Bitcoin fell as low as $59,540 in late Friday morning trading. At its current price, the digital coin is down 23% so far in November, putting it on pace for its worst monthly performance since June 2022 when it fell 38%, according to Yahoo Finance data.
The sell-off comes as chips and other tech stocks are tumbling on the heels of Anthropic's public debut, which investors largely viewed as the AI trade's 'Super Bowl moment' for 2026.
The monster listing has also ushered some soul-searching among crypto's longtime believers.
"I said back in May that most of the crypto industry was dead and it was never coming back. I believe that even more today," investor Anthony Pompliano said in a Friday post on X, where he remarked on the "enormous benefits" and " impressive revenue growth" of AI companies.
At its current pace, November is shaping up to be bitcoin's eighth-worst month since Yahoo Finance's daily records began in September 2014. Along with AI enthusiasm, which has prompted some bitcoin mining firms to sell their holdings at a faster pace, analysts have pointed to the toll that higher interest rates are taking on investor appetite for riskier assets.
- Ines Ferré
Anthropic stock extends losses, falls 12%
Anthropic (ANT) stock extended losses, dropping as much as 12% on Friday amid an overall AI trade meltdown.
Shares of the AI developer sank on their first full day of trading following the record-breaking IPO. Nearly every corner of the AI trade was under pressure on Friday, with semiconductors leading the way lower.
88.91 -8.26 (-8.50%)At close: November 20 at 4:00:02 PM EST87.79 -1.12 (-1.26%)After hours: 7:59:56 PM ESTAnthropic shares were trading near $86 each as of 10:55 a.m. ET. The company priced its initial public offering at $83 earlier this week, with shares opening at $111.50 on Thursday, but paring gains throughout the session.
- David Hollerith
The post earnings slide in Nvidia stock is getting uglier by the day
With Nvidia's (NVDA) stock falling another 3% Friday morning, the chip giant's post-earnings rout refuses to let up, Yahoo Finance's Brian Sozzi writes.
Shares of the fallen AI chip darling are down more than 10% since the company's Nov. 17 earnings report. The stock is down 14% since founder Jensen Huang resigned on Nov. 12 under a cloud of controversy, notably over his affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
Interim CEO and longtime CFO Colette Kress made a pretty compelling case this week that Nvidia can keep running the AI money machine without Huang in the driver's seat.
- David Hollerith
Stocks open mixed as AI trade weighs on heels of Anthropic debut.
US stocks were mixed Friday as the blue chip Dow Jones Industrial Index rose, while selling pressure continued across tech stocks on the heels of Anthropic's IPO.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI) climbed 0.5%, while the S&P 500 (^GSPC) declined by 0.5% and the Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC) fell 1.4%.
Anthropic (ANT) shares pulled back after surging in their public debut Thursday, while Nvidia (NVDA) extended its recent slide as weakness spread through semiconductor stocks. The S&P 500 entered Friday riding a six-session losing streak after all three major indexes dropped more than 2% Thursday.
Pressure was also visible beyond stocks, with gold futures sinking and bitcoin falling below $62,000. Investors will get another read on the consumer later Friday with the University of Michigan's final November sentiment survey.
48,147.33 -949.77 (-1.93%)At close: November 20 at 4:35:59 PM EST^DJI ^GSPC ^IXIC - Ines Ferré
Nvidia stock extends 6-day losing streak, as AMD, Broadcom lead chip sector lower
Chip giant Nvidia (NVDA) extended declines on Friday, heading for seven straight days of losses. Peers AMD (AMD) and Broadcom (AVGO) also tanked 6% and 3%, respectively. US-based chipmaker Intel (INTC) stock also declined.
Memory chipmaker Micron Technology (MU) and peer SK Hynix (SKHY) also dropped more than 3%.
The broader chip sector fell on Thursday following the public debut of AI model maker Anthropic (ANT). The sector was already on shaky ground following the exit of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and concerns over AI financing.
125.53 -20.45 (-14.01%)At close: November 20 at 4:00:01 PM EST130.01 +4.48 (+3.57%)After hours: 7:59:58 PM ESTNVDA AMD AVGOShares of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSM) and equipment maker ASML (ASML) fell as well, leading the Technology (XLK) sector lower.
Other areas of the AI trade were under pressure, with optical equipment maker Coherent (COHR) and Bloom Energy (BE) stocks sinking 6% and 7%, respectively.
- Brian Sozzi
Anthropic stock dives after rip-roaring IPO
Call it the Anthropic (ANT) IPO hangover.
Shares of the model builder dropped 13% in premarket trading on Friday as investors booked profits after a frenetic first day of trading. Not helping sentiment: The broader market plunged on Anthropic's well-received IPO day and remains under pressure today.
Anthropic made a monster debut on Wall Street Thursday, with shares opening at $111.50 a little before noon ET, a 34% premium to the $83 IPO price.
But the AI company's stock couldn't hold on to its early gains.
88.91 -8.26 (-8.50%)At close: November 20 at 4:00:02 PM EST87.79 -1.12 (-1.26%)After hours: 7:59:56 PM EST

The post earnings slide in Nvidia stock is getting uglier by the day
With Nvidia's (NVDA) stock falling another 3% Friday morning, the chip giant's post-earnings rout refuses to let up, Yahoo Finance's Brian Sozzi writes.

Shares of the fallen AI chip darling are down more than 10% since the company's Nov. 17 earnings report. The stock is down 14% since founder Jensen Huang resigned on Nov. 12 under a cloud of controversy, notably over his affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
Interim CEO and longtime CFO Colette Kress made a pretty compelling case this week that Nvidia can keep running the AI money machine without Huang in the driver's seat.

Stocks open mixed as AI trade weighs on heels of Anthropic debut.
US stocks were mixed Friday as the blue chip Dow Jones Industrial Index rose, while selling pressure continued across tech stocks on the heels of Anthropic's IPO.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI) climbed 0.5%, while the S&P 500 (^GSPC) declined by 0.5% and the Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC) fell 1.4%.

Anthropic (ANT) shares pulled back after surging in their public debut Thursday, while Nvidia (NVDA) extended its recent slide as weakness spread through semiconductor stocks. The S&P 500 entered Friday riding a six-session losing streak after all three major indexes dropped more than 2% Thursday.

Pressure was also visible beyond stocks, with gold futures sinking and bitcoin falling below $62,000. Investors will get another read on the consumer later Friday with the University of Michigan's final November sentiment survey.

Nvidia stock extends 6-day losing streak, as AMD, Broadcom lead chip sector lower

Chip giant Nvidia (NVDA) extended declines on Friday, heading for seven straight days of losses. Peers AMD (AMD) and Broadcom (AVGO) also tanked 6% and 3%, respectively. US-based chipmaker Intel (INTC) stock also declined.
Memory chipmaker Micron Technology (MU) and peer SK Hynix (SKHY) also dropped more than 3%.

The broader chip sector fell on Thursday following the public debut of AI model maker Anthropic (ANT). The sector was already on shaky ground following the exit of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and concerns over AI financing.

Anthropic stock dives after rip-roaring IPO
Call it the Anthropic (ANT) IPO hangover.

Shares of the model builder dropped 13% in premarket trading on Friday as investors booked profits after a frenetic first day of trading. Not helping sentiment: The broader market plunged on Anthropic's well-received IPO day and remains under pressure today.
Anthropic made a monster debut on Wall Street Thursday, with shares opening at $111.50 a little before noon ET, a 34% premium to the $83 IPO price.
But the AI company's stock couldn't hold on to its early gains.
